title.narrative: Provision of emergency lifesaving curative and preventive nutrition services among vulnerable populations in Afmadow District.

description.narrative: ltpgtWamo Relief and Rehabilitation Services (WRRS) proposes a 9-month nutrition project in Afmadow District, Lower Jubba, to address malnutrition and its underlying causes by implementing curative and preventive interventions. This project will focus on providing life-saving support to vulnerable populations across nine villages: Wabari , Camp Soya, Camp Bari, Camp Abaq-Bambow, Camp Yaq, Camp Abaq, Camp Gacanlow, Bulo Gumar, Bulo Weyn including ca Dhobley stabilization center through establishment of one static and three mobile teams.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project’s primary objective will be to reduce malnutrition related maternal morbidity and mortality by offering curative and preventive nutrition services targeting children under five years and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), while also building the capacity of the community to cope with climatic shocks. The project will adopt an integrated approach partnering with health and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) partners to provide a holistic package as guided by the UNICEF’s conceptual framework tackling both immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition.ltbrgtThe project will have two key components:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtMaternal infant and young child nutrition:lt/bgtltbrgtThis will mainly target the 1000 days of life with a focus on promoting the early initiation of breastfeeding, exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months, and appropriate complementary feeding practices based on age, frequency, consistency, and variety. Continued breastfeeding up to two years and beyond will also be promoted, alongside micronutrient supplementation and deworming services. To foster sustainable behavior change, the project will employ Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) strategies through one-on-one counseling and the establishment of mother-to-mother support (MTMSG) networks, empowering caregivers with knowledge and support to improve child nutrition outcomes. This will also promote kitchen gardening at the community level to promote dietary diversity and promote the one egg per day child per day campaign to promote uptake of eggs for children.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtIntegrated management of acute malnutrition:lt/bgtltbrgtThis will cover four components of IMAM: community mobilisation, stabilisation centre (SC), outpatient therapeutic programme(OTP) and targeted supplementary feeding programme (TSFP). Community mobilisation efforts will be through the community health workers (CHWs) and MTMSG network. Caregivers and CHWs will screen and refer children to the respective programmes with CHWs supporting in absentee and defaulter tracing.ltbrgtThe stabilization center and OTP will provide therapeutic feeding to children less than five years with severe acute malnutrition and with supplies from UNICEF and WHO. TSFP will focus on moderate acute malnutrition in children under five years and pregnant and lactating women with supplies received from WFP. Routine medication for both programs will be from UNICEF and SHF purchases. Handwashing soap and water treatment facilities for all beneficiaries in SC, OTP and TSFP will also be provided. This programme will be closely linked to health programme to provide EPI services and referrals from A/PNC to and from nutrition.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will also streamline the prevention of gender-based violence (GBV), Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Prevention of Diversion of Aid (PDAD), Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and child protection. WRRS will ensure these themes are mainstreamed throughout all activities to safeguard the well-being of beneficiaries and promote community trust and engagement.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will be implemented in line with the Somalia MoH, donor and international guidelines including in reporting. WSSR will coordinate and collaborate with national and state level actors by actively participating in cluster, subcluster and area-based coordination groups. Further, capacity building of staff, volunteers and community will form a key aspect of the project.ltbrgtlt/pgt
